key_insight: Geometry optimization of finite hyperbolic surface codes can significantly improve fault-tolerance efficiency, doubling code distance and quadrupling efficiency at fixed qubit count and parity-check weight.
engineering_relevance: The work supports modular quantum hardware design by showing how hyperbolic codes can be partitioned into bounded planar modules while reducing long-range routing demands.
method: Construct finite families of hyperbolic surface codes with optimized periodic identifications.
Analyze code performance under fixed qubit count, encoding rate, and parity-check weight.
Introduce a topology-aware routing algorithm for modular layouts.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level Monte Carlo simulations estimate finite-size thresholds for both modular and monolithic layouts and test the impact of tripling long-range gate error probability.
watch_item: The gains depend on topology-aware layout and routing, so practical benefits may be limited by hardware connectivity and long-range gate noise.
paper_title: Geometry-optimized hyperbolic codes for modular fault-tolerant quantum architectures
